messages:
jules: FYI forwarded customer email from Acme Payments — they asked for an SBOM snapshot and remediation ETA for CVE-2024-5678. They said it's flagged by their vendor risk scan and want a formal timeline for fixes and whether hosted API is impacted. marta: thanks — can you paste the exact excerpt from their scan? is it referencing libyaml or a transitive python dep? jules: quote from Acme: 'CVE-2024-5678 affecting pyyaml < 6.0 found in dependency tree; please confirm presence in your runtime, provide SBOM and expected remediation date.' They want SOC2 evidence pack items too (evidence of patching process). cve-bot: New advisory: CVE-2024-5678 - pyyaml unsafe_load issue. Upstream fixed in 6.0. Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-5678 alex: quick check — hosted inference runtime image (redwood/runtime:prod-2024.11) vendors a frozen python environment for control-plane tasks. The tokenization/generation engine is C++ and not affected. But some support services (ingest, eval harness) use pyyaml. need to confirm which images contain pyyaml.
marta: action items: 1) confirm which internal images include vulnerable pyyaml 2) determine whether hosted customers have exposure vs private (customer) deployments 3) produce SBOM snapshot for hosted runtime 4) provide remediation ETA and SOC2 evidence checklist to Acme. dan: I spun a quick scan on container registry: `trivy image redwood/runtime-support:2024-11` shows pyyaml 5.4.1 present in /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages. So the support-image is affected. Hosted API frontends are not. alex: thanks Dan. Plan: bump pyyaml to 6.0 in support image, rebuild and push, then run integration tests. I can do a hotfix branch and image build today — estimate: build+CI 6-8 hours, internal rollout 24 hours for canary, full rollout 48 hours after validation. Total ETA ~3 business days for full remediation. marta: good. For SOC2 evidence they usually want: patch ticket, date applied, rollouts, and SBOM before/after. We should generate SBOMs for the current hosted images and the patched images. I can prepare a remediation statement template. jules: customer asked if remediation will affect service availability. what do we tell them? alex: no downtime expected — it's a non-breaking support-image update. We'll rotate containers gradually. We can offer a mitigation: for private deployments, recommend customers upgrade images or apply the patched container. For hosted, we will apply patch ourselves. marta: timeline for communication: draft to Acme by EOD today with: - confirmation of affected components (support services only) - SBOM snapshot (attached as tar) - remediation ETA (~3 business days) - statement about no expected downtime - SOC2 evidence next steps (we'll provide patch ticket and SBOMs). Who can take point on the customer-facing message? jules: I'll take point. please drop the SBOM and ticket links here when available. alex: I'll open a GH issue: `infra/patches#482` — will include build logs and CI run. patch PR coming in 30m. cve-bot: Suggested mitigation: restrict YAML parsing input or replace unsafe_load usage. See internal security playbook: /docs/sec/playbooks/yaml_hardening.md dan: note for on-prem/private customers: if they manage their own images we need to provide the patched image and upgrade notes. I'll prepare a short runbook for Private customers (how to rotate runtime images and verify checksums). marta: excellent. follow-ups: alex attach PR link, dan attach runbook, jules draft email. I'll start the SOC2 evidence checklist and export current SBOMs (CycloneDX) from registry. alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/271 (hotfix/pyyaml-6.0). Build passed on linux-x86 and linux-arm, pushing images now. jules: formatting email draft below — please review: > Hi Acme team, > Thanks for flagging CVE-2024-5678. We confirmed pyyaml 5.4.1 is present in our internal support image used for ingestion/eval tasks and not in the hosted generation runtime. We will deploy a hotfix to replace pyyaml with 6.0. Estimated full remediation: 3 business days. No service downtime expected. We will provide SBOM snapshots and patch ticket evidence when available. marta: fine, small tweak: change 'not in the hosted generation runtime' -> 'not in the hosted inference generation runtime' to be explicit. Also add contact for private deployment instructions. jules: updated and sent. customer replied: 'Thanks — please send SBOM and ticket link when ready. Also, can you confirm whether KMS keys or any key material was impacted?' alex: KMS unaffected. The CVE is a parsing issue in pyyaml, not crypto; no key material touched. Add that to reply. marta: I'll attach SBOM export here when done and add the SOC2 evidence checklist items: - GH issue #271 (patch PR) - registry digest with patched image - CycloneDX SBOM before/after - validation test matrix + dates dan: runbook saved: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/private-image-upgrade (short checklist + verification commands). alex: pushed patched image: `registry.redwood/runtime-support:2024-11-hotfix-pyyaml6` digest sha256:abcd1234... marta: SBOMs attached in ticket. I'm packaging evidence PDF. ETA to customer for final package: tomorrow morning (UTC). jules: customer replied: 'Got it, thanks. We'll close the finding once we receive SBOM + ticket evidence.' :thumbsup: marta: closing notes: mark CVE triage as complete in internal tracker, link to PR/registry/SBOMs. Good teamwork. alex: closing the PR now. dan: adding post-mortem note to vuln tracker: recommend adding pyyaml upgrade guard to dependency checker to catch <6.0 automatically. jules: thanks all — I'll file the customer evidence email thread in the support ticket and set the expected remediation date in the CRM.
